chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of marrying the Zanj, for they are a disfigured creation.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.نِكَاحَ الزِّنْجِ: Marriage to the Zanj (people of East Africa/Sudan)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying the Zanj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) advises avoiding marriage with the Zanj, characterizing them as 'khalq mushawwah' (disfigured creation). While classical scholars often interpreted this as a reference to distinct physical traits or specific lineage qualities, Shia exegetes also debate whether it denotes a temporary condition or a permanent attribute, linking it to broader themes of physical and spiritual purity in marital selection.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Ziyad, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘Beware of marrying (the people of) Al-Zanj, (a coastal region of Africa) for these are disfigured creatures’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali has narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Ziyad who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ’You must remain on your guard against marriage with people of al-Zanj because it is a distorted creature.’”
